breast cancer patients receiving chemotherapy. The partic-
ipants attended about 70% of their supervised exercise
sessions, which is within the range commonly reported for
breast cancer patients receiving adjuvant therapy [3] and older
adults without cancer [8]. For the 30% of supervised exercise
sessions that were missed, breast cancer patients reported 36
different exercise barriers. The top seven barriers—feeling
sick, fatigue, loss of interest, vacation, nausea/vomiting, work
issues, and pain—accounted for over 50% of all missed
exercise sessions. Organizing these barriers into higher-order
accounted for over 50% of all missed exercise sessions.
Moreover, of the participants who missed multiple exercise
sessions, 67% reported three or more different barriers to
exercise and 31% reported five or more different barriers.
Lastly, demographic, medical, and exercise/health variables
did not predict the types of exercise barriers reported.
As hypothesized, our data show that disease/treatment-
related barriers accounted for over 50% of all missed
exercise sessions. It is clear from these data that addressing
the side effects of chemotherapy is the critical issue for
improving exercise adherence during breast cancer chemo-
therapy. What is unclear, however, is the extent to which
these barriers can be addressed with behavioral interven-
tions. Some barriers, such as fatigue, may be managed
behaviorally by prescribing low-to-moderate intensity ex-
ercise (e.g., 50–60% of maximal capacity), allowing shorter
duration exercise (e.g., 10 min at a time), performing
interval exercise (i.e., alternating exercise and rest bouts),
and exercising when fatigue is at its lowest (e.g., early in
the morning or on certain days in the chemotherapy cycle).
Similarly, strategies to overcome the barrier of diarrhea may
include lower intensity and shorter duration exercise, not
exercising after meals, and exercising in locations where
washrooms are convenient and private (e.g., at home) rather
than sparse and public (e.g., outdoor walking trails, fitness
